title: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: His father Rav Ika lived in Abaye’s time, as in Avodah Zarah 65a, and married the sister of Rav Acha bar Yaakov, who bore him Rav Acha, as in Ketubot 74a, where they said: “Rav Acha bar Yaakov said that Rabbi Yochanan said … Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, his sister’s son, raised an objection to him … he said to him: Student, you have spoken well?”

Hyman places him in his uncle’s town and considers it beyond doubt that he received from him, as in Eruvin 63a: Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia and Rav Acha bar Tachlifa visited the house of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika in the place of Rav Acha bar Yaakov. He wanted to prepare a choice calf [עיגלא תילתא] for them; he brought a knife and showed it to them. Rav Acha bar Tachlifa said to him: “Should we not be concerned for the elder?” (that is, Rav Acha bar Yaakov, who was very old and was Rav Huna’s student). It is known that Rav Acha bar Yaakov’s place was Papunya, as in Kiddushin 35a. We find in Keritot 3b that he spoke in the name of Rav Bivi bar Abaye. He was Rav Papa’s colleague, as in Shabbat 6a, where he resolved Rav Papa’s difficulty; in Nedarim 30a he disagrees with Rav Papa. In Rav Ashi’s academy he was a leading sage of the generation, disagreeing with Rav Ashi about Rav Bivi’s words, as in Makkot 21b; in Bava Kamma 74 he said to Rav Ashi, “Rava’s inference — from where?”; and in Chullin 112b he raised a difficulty against Rav Ashi.

And what we find in Nazir 42a, that he said “This says that the majority is like the whole by Torah law,” and Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina challenged it, “This is written of an impure nazirite” — Seder HaDorot wondered at this: was not Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina much earlier than Rav Acha son of Rav Ika? Hyman regards this as no difficulty at all, for Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina does not refer to Rav Acha’s exposition but to the mishnah that two hairs prevent [completion], as they said there in Tosafot: “Rabbi Chanina challenges.” And if the verse refers only to an impure nazirite, Rav Acha’s exposition still applies, to say that the majority is like the whole by Torah law. He regards this as clear.

His halakhot remain to us through the mouth of his student Rav Huna bar Manoach, who always spoke in his name, as in Megillah 25b, Gittin 24a and 64b, Bava Kamma 58b, Bava Metzia 71b and Sanhedrin 42a. He is likewise mentioned in Yevamot 54a and 90a, Nazir 51b, Kiddushin 27b, Bava Kamma 47a, Bava Metzia 77b, Sanhedrin 53b, Avodah Zarah 34b, Bekhorot 28b and 45a, and Keritot 3b.

notes.text: The uncle is Acha barYaakov through Ika’s wife, retained explicitly. עיגלא תילתא is a choice calf; the draft’s third-grown was unsupported. Hyman’s Papunya and chronology arguments remain attributed. The Nazir objection is assigned by Hyman to the Mishnah, not a personal encounter across generations; the always and clear force are preserved.

The consulted Makkot 21b has Acha son of Ika demonstrate Bivi’s dictum and Ashi give a different view. Nazir 42a places Acha’s majority inference and Yose bar Chanina’s objection in the surrounding two-hair discussion; Hyman’s specific Tosafot-based assignment of the objection and chronological reconciliation remain attributed. The maternal uncle, choice calf, always transmission and clear-force conclusions remain intact.
